subject: Dedicated capacity: queueing & throughput addendum negotiation
messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@clearsight.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@clearsight.ai
Date: 2027-09-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity – queueing and throughput questions

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the Dedicated pool for our inference workloads, the architecture team asked for a more concrete statement on how Redwood handles:

- sustained burst load (short spikes where 40% of requests are batch scoring, rest are low-latency chat requests)
- queueing behavior when reserved GPUs are saturated (do you preempt background jobs? priority queues?)
- how you measure and credit for shortfalls against promised throughput (do we get credits or auto-burst to shared capacity?)

We attached a sample traffic trace (CS_traffic_profile_Q2.csv) — that represents the kind of diurnal + weekday spikes we see. Our procurement and infra teams need a clear carveout or addendum for any latency outages tied to tenant-isolation or prioritization.

Can you outline the recommended SLA addendum language (preferred P95/P99 latency targets by class, a queue-depth carveout, and any burst forgiveness window)? If you can draft a redline we can circulate internally, that would be ideal.

Best,
Priya
Priya Menon
VP, Cloud Ops | ClearSight Analytics

Attachments: CS_traffic_profile_Q2.csv (csv)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@clearsight.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-11T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity – queueing and throughput questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the trace and for outlining the ask. I reviewed the file and sketched a pragmatic SLA addendum that balances isolation with predictable economics. Key points (high level):

• Reservation model: you get reserved capacity expressed as "reserved GPUs" (N GPUs) with a soft headroom burst pool for short spikes (configurable: 5–20% of commit) that we allow for up to a 10-minute rolling window per hour.

• Priority queueing: latency-sensitive request types (chat/interactive) are tagged and placed in a prioritized lane. Best-effort/background batch scoring is queued to a lower-priority lane and can be preempted during sustained contention.

• Queue-depth carveout: for traffic surges exceeding the 99th-percentile of your historical request rate by >3x sustained for >15 minutes, latency SLOs convert to a "degraded mode" for that window; in degraded mode we commit to preserving interactive P95 (but not P99) and apply credits for P99 misses per the addendum.

• Throughput shortfalls & credits: credits calculated on per-minute shortfall of token throughput vs committed tokens/min, capped at X% monthly. We also provide automatic fallback to our hosted burst pool (subject to availability) during defined maintenance or extreme overloads — fallback is opt-in in the addendum.

I attached a draft addendum (draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf) and a redline template (sla_redline_cs_v1.docx). They include suggested thresholds and sample clause language you can hand to procurement.

If this aligns with you, I can run it by our pricing and legal teams and propose minor language adjustments (credit caps and DSLA formula). Would you prefer to keep the burst pool opt-in or make it default with a surcharge?

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Strategic Cloud Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (pdf), sla_redline_cs_v1.docx (docx)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity – queueing and throughput questions (ClearSight)

Marissa/Diego — forwarding Priya's request and my proposed addendum. Key asks:

1) Approve a default 10-minute burst window at up to 15% of committed GPUs for a surcharge tier (we can price).
2) Approve queueing behavior: prioritized interactive lane, preemptible batch lane. Need confirmation on how far we push preemption (kill vs suspend).
3) Confirm credit formula: I'm proposing credits equal to 5x the per-minute shortfall (in $) up to 20% monthly cap; legal may push that down.

Please reply with edits or "+1" so I can return to Priya with a firm stance. I'm happy to host a 30-min technical call if needed.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated capacity – queueing and throughput questions (ClearSight)

+1 on the overall approach. A couple of operational notes from runtime:

- Preemption model: we should avoid hard-killing in-progress batch scoring; instead we checkpoint and move to a suspended cold queue. We can signal clients with a 429+Retry-After when suspension happens.
- Latency targets: preserve interactive P95 at committed concurrency; set interactive P99 as a best-effort with credit triggers only after 15 consecutive minutes of degradation.
- Monitoring: recommend a shared observability hook (read-only token) so ClearSight can see per-route queue depth and the KV cache hit-rate that drives tail latency.

I think the credit multiplier can be 4x rather than 5x to reduce financial exposure; legal will want a monetary cap anyway. Marissa — any objections on the monitoring clause?

—Diego
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: 2027-09-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Dedicated capacity addendum (ClearSight)

Hi Priya — thanks for your patience. Per internal review we've agreed to the following defaults for the addendum:

• Burst window: default opt-in 10-minute burst (up to 15% reserved GPU headroom), surcharge applies; you can opt-out to keep pricing lower.
• Queueing: prioritized interactive lane; batch scoring is suspended (checkpointed) not hard-killed. When suspension occurs we will return 429 + Retry-After to the client.
• Degraded mode: traffic surges >3x 99th-percentile sustained >15 minutes push the tenant into degraded mode; interactive P95 remains protected.
• Credits: credit multiplier set to 4x per-minute shortfall with a 15% monthly cap (legal requested the lower cap).
• Monitoring: we will grant ClearSight a read-only observability token scoped to per-route queue depth, KV cache hit-rate, and token throughput metrics.

I've attached the redline (sla_redline_cs_v1.docx) and a final PDF of the addendum (draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf). If that looks good I'll send the DocuSign link to your procurement contact (link: https://docusign.net/link/AA1B2C3D-clear-sight-sla).

If you want a quick 30-min tech sync to walk through the trace and the monitoring dashboard, happy to schedule next week.

Best,
Nikhil
Account Executive, Strategic Cloud Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf, sla_redline_cs_v1.docx
